question: Evidence linking benzo[a]pyrene exposure with female breast cancer incidence

limitations: meat-based exposure is not whole-diet or contaminated-oil BaP

diet_E3N_2025.checked: publisher and primary indexed abstracts; complete tables not obtained
limitations: do not attribute PAH4 result solely to BaP
estimated food intake combined with French total-diet contamination data

air_E3N_2021.checked: publisher abstract and indexed primary tables
limitations: ambient modeled exposure not cooking-fume or oil exposure
correlated pollutants and residual confounding possible

air_E3N_trajectories_2024.result: No association with BaP trajectory classes; positive PCB153 result
limitations: same parent E3N population as 2021; not independent replication

animal_oral_1995.dose: 50 micromol per rat per week for 8 weeks, gavage in trioctanoin
animal_oral_1995.result: mammary adenocarcinoma incidence significantly higher than vehicle
limitations: high experimental dose; cannot transfer incidence or dose-response to daily low-dose human oil consumption

mechanism_2025.model: T47D breast cancer cell line, NOT normal primary mammary cells
mechanism_2025.result: DNA/protein adduct formation; reactive metabolite transfer supports mechanistic plausibility
limitations: not proof of transformation of normal cells

synthesis: Mammary carcinogenic potential is supported experimentally; human BaP-specific dietary associations remain inconsistent. No inference of a Taiwan oil-event causal effect or dose-specific risk can be made from these studies alone.
